sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 3

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 3:1
items.html:
In it, it explains the ten Sefirot whose level is equal. And it contains five matters: 1. In every place through which the spiritual passes, it acquires its place there. Therefore all the lower Sefirot remain in the upper ones, because they passed through them. 2. The ten Sefirot of direct light and the ten Sefirot of reflected light stand in reverse order. 3. The ten Sefirot of reflected light completed each and every Sefira into ten Sefirot. 4. The Malchut of reflected light, who joined with the Keter of direct light, acquired the level of Keter; and since she passed through all the Sefirot, they all attained the level of Keter. 5. That ten Sefirot emerged in length and ten Sefirot in thickness.

Now we shall explain the ten Sefirot whose level is equal. That is, if the level of the coupling reaches Keter, there are in it 100 Sefirot — namely ten Sefirot from Keter to Malchut in thickness, clothing one upon the other, each of which has ten Sefirot in length, from Keter to Malchut. And if the level of the coupling reaches Hochma, they have nine Sefirot in thickness, each of which has nine Sefirot in length. And if the level of the coupling reaches Bina, they have eight Sefirot in thickness, each of which has eight Sefirot in length, and so forth in this manner. And this applies in each and every coupling by striking of the upper light upon the screen, which is brought in the words of the ARI here in Chapter 1.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 3:2
items.html: And the reason is that wherever it is said that a spiritual thing passes from place to place, the meaning is not that it left the first place and came to a second place, in the manner of corporeal things; rather, there is here only a phase of addition, for the whole of it remains in the first place just as it was, even after it has come to the second place. Thus it turns out that a second place has been added to it as well, for there is no absence in spirituality (as the ARI writes in Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sawing, Chapter 7). And since the Sefira of Keter is the root of the four phases HB TM of direct light, they necessarily pass through it; and if so, they have left their root in it, for the reason that there is no absence in spirituality. Therefore there are necessarily in the Sefira of Keter alone all nine Sefirot, KHB HGT NHY of direct light. And in the same way in the Sefira of Hochma, through which Bina and TM passed: they have fixed their place in her, and there are in the Sefira of Hochma eight Sefirot, from Hochma to Yesod. And in the same way in Bina, through which TM passed and fixed their place in her, and there are in Bina seven Sefirot, from Bina to Yesod; and likewise in the HGT NHY that are in Tifferet, and likewise in Malchut. Thus Keter is incorporated of nine Sefirot, KHB HGT NHY of direct light — that is, apart from Malchut, for in Malchut there is no direct light, but reflected light alone. And Hochma is incorporated of eight Sefirot, HB HGT NHY of direct light. And Bina is incorporated of seven Sefirot: Bina, HGT NHY of direct light. And Hesed is incorporated of six Sefirot, HGT NHY of direct light. And so forth in this manner, so that every upper Sefira is incorporated of all the lower Sefirot that passed within her, for the reason that there is no absence in spirituality (and this has already been explained in Part 2, Inner Observation, Chapter 9).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 3:3
items.html: And now, this incorporation of which we have spoken came about by the force of the ten Sefirot KHB TM of direct light themselves, even before the coupling by striking was made upon the screen that raises reflected light and clothes them. However, after the coupling by striking was made upon the screen in Malchut, and the reflected light ascended from the screen in Malchut and clothed the Sefirot of direct light, then the reflected light makes the level of them all equal. For example, if the coupling was upon a screen of phase four, which raises reflected light up to Keter, then ten Sefirot of reflected light emerged here — KHB HGT NHYM — from Malchut, and clothed the KHB HGT NHY of direct light. And the ten Sefirot of reflected light are found in the reverse order of the ten Sefirot of direct light, for the ten Sefirot of direct light have their root above, in Keter, and are found standing from above downward, from Keter to Yesod; whereas the ten Sefirot of reflected light have their root in Malchut, since they emerged from her, and they are discerned as standing from below upward. For the Keter of reflected light — that is, the root — is in Malchut; and the Hochma of reflected light is in the Yesod of direct light; and the Bina of reflected light is in the Hod of direct light; and the Hesed of reflected light is in the Netzah of direct light; and the Gevura of reflected light is in the Tifferet of direct light; and the Tifferet of reflected light is in the Gevura of direct light; and the Netzah of reflected light is in the Hesed of direct light; and the Hod of reflected light is in the Bina of direct light; and the Yesod of reflected light is in the Hochma of direct light; and the Malchut of reflected light is in the Keter of direct light. Thus they stand from below upward, beginning with Malchut and ending with Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 3:4
items.html: And when the ten Sefirot of reflected light join with the ten Sefirot of direct light, ten Sefirot are found in each one. For Malchut, who had nothing at all of direct light, gained ten complete Sefirot of reflected light, from Keter to Malchut, since they all passed through her and remained in her permanently, for the reason that there is no absence in spirituality. And the Yesod of direct light, which had no more than a single Sefira of direct light, has now attained nine Sefirot from the reflected light, from Hochma to Malchut, since they all passed through it. And the Hod of direct light, which had no more than two Sefirot, has now attained eight Sefirot from the reflected light, from Bina to Malchut. And the Netzah of direct light, which had three Sefirot, attained seven Sefirot, from Hesed to Malchut. And so forth in this manner, until Hochma of direct light, who had eight Sefirot of direct light — HB HGT NHY — has now attained the Yesod and Malchut of reflected light and was completed into ten Sefirot. And Keter of direct light, which had nine Sefirot, KHB HGT NHY of direct light, has now attained the Malchut of reflected light and was completed into ten Sefirot.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 3:5
items.html: And thus the Malchut of reflected light attained the level of Keter, since she joined with the Keter of direct light. And the Yesod of reflected light attained the level of Hochma, since it joined with the Hochma of direct light. And Hod attained the level of Bina, because it joined with Bina. And so forth. Therefore it is discerned that the Hochma of direct light too attained the level of Keter; for that same Malchut of reflected light which joined with Keter and became the level of Keter passed through Hochma and was fixed in her, and if so, Hochma too attained the level of Keter through her. And likewise the Bina of direct light attained the level of Keter, for the Yesod and Malchut of reflected light, which became Hochma and Keter, passed on their way through her and left their root in her. And in the same way each and every Sefira of direct light attained the level of Keter, because the Malchut of reflected light that joined with Keter necessarily passed within them and was fixed in her. Thus, after the reflected light ascended and joined with the direct light, all the Sefirot were made equal in an equal level, up to Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 3:6
items.html: And it is discerned that that same incorporation — by which each and every Sefira was incorporated of ten Sefirot through the joining of direct light and reflected light — stands in thickness, and they clothe one upon the other; and this is by reason of their equal level. Thus, innermost of them all stand the ten Sefirot of Keter in length, from Keter to Malchut; and upon them, in thickness, clothe the ten Sefirot of Hochma, which stand in length from Keter to Malchut; and upon them clothe the ten Sefirot of Bina, from Keter to Malchut, and so forth, until the ten Sefirot that are in Malchut clothe upon the externality of them all, from Keter to Malchut. And so it has been explained that from every coupling by striking of the upper light upon a screen of phase four, 100 Sefirot must emerge — that is, ten Sefirot in length, each of which expands into ten Sefirot in thickness, and the level of them all is equal, up to Keter. And in the same way, in a coupling by striking upon a screen of phase three, nine Sefirot emerge in length and nine Sefirot in thickness, whose level is equal, up to Hochma. And in the same way, in a coupling by striking of phase two, eight Sefirot emerge in length and eight Sefirot in thickness, whose level is equal, up to Bina. And so forth in this manner.
